title: The Sasquatch Defense
logline: Brad Morris recruits Marshall as the human wall for his team in the Bar League, Manhattan's lawyers-only laser tag league, and twenty years of Bigfoot hunting turn out to have made Marshall invisible. When Marshall won't switch firms to stay on the team, Brad's favor becomes a grudge match for the Golden Gavel against Marshall's hastily hired paralegals: Ted, Robin, Lily and a Barney who cannot stop glowing.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2012, your Uncle Marshall became the most feared man in the New York legal community. Not in a courtroom. In a warehouse on Thirty-Ninth Street, wearing a vest that beeped.

couch.line: For about two Thursdays. Then he met someone scarier.

guests.name: Marjorie Kettle
guests.role: the Bar League's referee, a court stenographer of thirty-one years who takes down everything said in the arena and reads it back, flat and verbatim, at the worst possible moment

scenes.summary: Brad recruits Marshall as the 'wall' for his Bar League laser tag team, the Habeas Corpses. Barney is territorial about his sport; Brad reveals he's a Civil War reenactor. Flashback: Brad sat next to lonely Marshall on day one of law school and claimed to love Bigfoot. Marshall agrees. The gang bets on how fast he'll be tagged. Button: Barney has taken a job at a rival firm to be there.

beats.line: Brad Morris asked me to meet him here. He says he needs a favor.
Last time Brad needed a favor, he took your client, your parking space and your stapler.
He gave the stapler back.
And billed you for the staples.
Marsh. Gang. I'll cut right to it. Marsh, have you ever played laser tag?
Excuse me?
Not you, Barney.
The Bar League. Manhattan lawyers only. Thursday nights, in a blacklit warehouse on Thirty-Ninth Street.
Is it a bar league because it's lawyers, or because it's next to a bar?
Yes.
My team is the Habeas Corpses. Six seasons. Never won the Golden Gavel.
Habeas Corpses. That's the best thing a lawyer has ever said at this table.
Our big guy, Dworkin, made partner. Now he says he's too valuable to get shot.
So I need a new wall. Someone huge, slow and loud, who soaks up fire while we flank.
And I thought, who's the hugest, slowest, loudest guy I know?
Brad. You thought of me?
Absolutely not. Laser tag is a Stinson sport. James and I have been at war since 1987.
I have a framed photo of my high score in my bathroom. Not the guest bathroom. Mine.
No offense, Barney, you're a showboat. Laser tag is strategy. I'm a Civil War reenactor.
Union. Twentieth Maine. I've died at Gettysburg eleven times.
So you're an expert at dying.
At dying well, Robin. Huge difference.
Brad, I don't know. I'm not really a laser tag guy.
Marsh. First day of law school. Who sat next to you?
Kids, on Marshall's first day at Columbia Law, nobody wanted to sit next to the giant from Minnesota.
Bro. You're enormous. Study partners? I'll do the outlines, you scare off the gunners.
Yes! I'm Marshall. From Minnesota. Do you like Bigfoot?
Love Bigfoot.
He did not love Bigfoot.
Okay. So. Nineteen sixty-seven. Bluff Creek, California. A man with a camera—
You did sit next to me.
And who carried you through Contracts?
You did.
And who borrowed your Torts notes and never gave them back?
Also you.
Teamwork.
Okay. I'm in. I'll be your wall.
Thursday, nine. Wear dark colors. Don't eat first. Our last wall threw up in the bunker.
I give him ninety seconds.
Thirty.
He'll apologize to every single person who shoots him.
That's just manners, Lily!
Four seconds. And I'll be there. I just got hired as a paralegal at Glickman and Glickman. Thursdays, seven to nine.
Barney, you can't just get a job so you can play laser tag.
Robin. How do you think I got my real one?

scenes.summary: Thursday. Brad's plan is Pickett's Charge with Marshall as the target. Marjorie the stenographer-referee reads back trash talk; Barney arrives for the other team in a shirt that glows under blacklight. Montage: Marshall vanishes. Final: Marshall 61 tags, never hit; Barney hit 44 times, 41 in the shirt. Marshall explains twenty years of Bigfoot hunting. Then rule nine: players must work at the firm. Brad has a job offer ready; Marshall refuses; the win is vacated, and Brad declares war. Button: Barney asks to be taught invisibility, glowing.

beats.line: Every Thursday, the meanest lawyers in Manhattan settled their differences with lasers. Technically, infrared.
Okay, Marsh. Tonight we run Pickett's Charge.
Brad, Pickett's Charge was the worst disaster of the whole Civil War.
For Pickett. I was on the other side, bro. Eleven times.
You walk straight up the middle. Big. Loud. Everybody shoots you. Then we flank.
So my whole job is getting shot.
Marsh, you are gonna get shot so much. It's gonna be beautiful.
Habeas Corpses versus Glickman and Glickman. I'm Marjorie. I referee.
Thirty-one years a court stenographer. Anything you say in this arena, I take down. Anything.
No trash talk. Last season she read one back at a guy's deposition.
Glickman and Glickman's newest paralegal has arrived. Daddy's home.
Barney, your shirt is glowing.
Marshall. I am always glowing.
Quote. I am always glowing. Unquote.
This is my sport, Eriksen. Four seconds.
Quote. Four seconds. Unquote. Lights down.

beats.label: Habeas Corpses vs. Glickman and Glickman

beats.line: Wall! Go! Draw their fire!
Wall? Where's my wall?
Something's out there. It smells like pine. And ranch.
Be the tree, Marshall. Be the tree.
Who keeps shooting me in the shirt?
Marsh? Buddy? Are you even in here?
Final. Habeas Corpses win. Their first win in six seasons.
Six seasons, Marsh!
Brad Morris, four tags. Marshall Eriksen, sixty-one tags. Times Eriksen was hit, zero.
Barney Stinson, hit forty-four times. Forty-one in the shirt.
That's impossible. Nobody even saw him!
Marsh. How?
Brad, I've spent twenty years in the Minnesota woods looking for something that doesn't want to be seen.
Somewhere along the way, I picked up a few of his moves.
Bro. You're a Sasquatch.
I have waited my whole life for someone to say that.
Before I certify. Rule nine. Every player must work at the team's firm. Mister Eriksen, where do you work?
Oh. Not at Brad's firm.
Way ahead of you. HR drafted an offer last night. In case you were good.
Brad, I'm an environmental lawyer. I protect wetlands.
We have wetlands! We represent a parking lot that used to be one.
No.
Then the win is vacated.
Marsh. Our first win in six seasons.
I'm sorry, Brad. I'm not switching firms over laser tag.
Cool. Totes cool. No hard feelings, bro.
See you at the Golden Gavel, counselor.
But my firm doesn't even have a team.
Five players. One licensed attorney. Registration closes Friday.
Marshall. I quit Glickman. Teach me how to be invisible.
Buddy, I can see you from Minnesota.

scenes.summary: First practice of Sasquatch and Associates in Barney's office. Ted is pedantic about infrared and the arena's ceiling; Robin refuses to say pew; Marshall teaches the three rules; Lily says nobody ever sees her coming. Barney debuts the all-black Midnight suit, but his teeth glow and he can't stop smiling; the stillness drill breaks him. Brad delivers a hostile brunch and a scouting report with nothing on Lily, reveals he listened to three years of Bigfoot, and is bringing his corgi. Button: Robin on corgis.

beats.line: So Marshall hired four paralegals, at a dollar each. Barney negotiated up to a dollar fifty.
Welcome to the first practice of Sasquatch and Associates.
Point of order. Laser tag uses infrared. Technically, we're an infrared tag team.
Technically, you'll be the first one I tag.
Marshall, I own four real guns. I'm not pointing a flashlight with self-esteem at a tax attorney.
Robin, you're our sharpshooter. You don't have to love the gun.
Fine. But I am not saying pew.
I've also studied the arena's floor plan. The sight lines are criminal. Whoever designed it hates people.
Ted, it's a warehouse.
Exactly. Nobody even tried.
The Sasquatch method has three rules. One. Be still. Two. Be silent.
Three. Be the tree.
What kind of tree?
A quiet one, Ted.
Lilypad, you haven't asked a single question.
I don't need training, Marshmallow. Every spring I take twenty kindergartners through the Museum of Natural History.
I've never lost one. And not one of them has ever seen me coming.
Behold. The Midnight. Black suit, black shirt, black tie. Even the lining is in mourning.
Barney, it's great. But under blacklight, teeth glow. Every time you smile, you're a lighthouse.
Then I won't smile.
You're smiling right now.
Because I'm picturing how awesome I'll look not smiling.
Stillness drill. Everybody freeze. One minute. No moving, no talking.
Nobody's looking at me. Is this what Ted's whole life feels like?
Knock knock. Professional courtesy. Blueberry muffins in the lobby, and a scouting report.
It's a hostile brunch, Marsh.
Ted Mosby. Talks during games. Mostly about the ceiling.
It's exposed ductwork painted black, Brad! As if that hides it!
Robin Scherbatsky. Refuses to say pew.
I said that ninety seconds ago.
I have a guy.
Barney Stinson. Glows.
Like a god.
Lily Aldrin.
Huh. Nothing. I've got literally nothing on Lily.
But you, Marsh? Three years of law school, you talked about Bigfoot. I listened to every word.
Squatch moves at dusk. Squatch avoids dogs. Squatch cannot resist ranch dressing.
Brad, that last one was never about Bigfoot.
See you Thursday, Sasquatch. Oh, and I'm bringing Hollandaise.
Wait. Brad listened to three years of Bigfoot? Dad, is this a love story?
Penny, every story about Uncle Marshall is a love story. Most of them are about sandwiches.
Guys. He's bringing the corgi.
Marshall, it's a corgi. It's a loaf of bread that hates you.

scenes.summary: The Golden Gavel, mid-game. Ted is tagged mid-rant about the ceiling. Robin goes nine tags and gets read back saying pew. The corgi eats a vest. Barney achieves perfect stillness and is tagged in the teeth on 'Legen'. Down to Marshall versus Brad, with one mystery teammate still in. Face to face, Brad admits he never cared about the gavel: he missed his friend. Marjorie reads back 'I hate Bigfoot'. They make a brunch date and hug, and Lily, silent all game, tags them both. Future Ted: Marshall finally found the creature nobody sees coming.

beats.line: Robin. Look at this ceiling. Exposed ductwork, painted black, as if that hides it.
Ted. Be the tree.
I'm just saying, a little honesty in a ceiling would really—
Mosby. Tagged. By Scherbatsky.
Robin!
I told you you'd be first.
Come on out, Corpses! Canadians don't hide behind bunkers!
Scherbatsky. Nine tags. And tagged.
Nine tags. And I never once said pew.
Quote. Pew pew pew. Eat that, you billable hour. Unquote.
That's out of context.
Marsh! Hollandaise is in the building!
The corgi has been removed from the arena. She ate a vest.
She was hungry, Marjorie!
Marshall. I'm doing it. Two minutes. Still. Silent. Completely invisible.
This is going to be legen... wait for it...
Stinson. Tagged in the teeth.
Dary.
Habeas Corpses, one player left. Sasquatch and Associates, two.
Two? Who else is still in?
I'm not at liberty to say.
Marsh, I know you're behind the blue bunker. I can smell the ranch.
Dang it.
Brad. Why do you want this so bad? It's a plastic gavel.
It's not the gavel, Marsh. Since you went environmental, I only see you across a conference table.
I ask you to brunch, you're in Minnesota. I ask again, you're in court. Against me.
So I figured if I couldn't get you to brunch, I'd get you to a war.
Brad. You sat through three years of Bigfoot.
Bro. I hate Bigfoot.
I just liked sitting next to you.
Quote. I hate Bigfoot. Unquote.
I'm gonna need a minute on that first part.
Brad, you could have just said you missed me.
Marsh, I'm a litigator. I don't say things. I file them.
Brunch. Sunday. Bring Hollandaise.
Aldrin. Two tags. Game.
Sorry, boys. You were both standing very still.
Where did she even come from? I didn't have a single note on her!
Brad, she was standing right in front of me. The whole game.
Sasquatch and Associates win the Golden Gavel. Most valuable player, Lily Aldrin. Paralegal.
Kids, Brad and Marshall had brunch every Sunday after that. Brad never brought up Bigfoot. Marshall never stopped.
Uncle Marshall spent twenty years hunting a creature nobody ever sees coming. He'd been married to her since 2007.
